sentiment.rationale: Forward guidance was meaningfully raised: full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA is guided to grow 8-10% (to $5.8-$5.9 billion) versus 8% growth in 2025, adjusted EPS is guided to grow 13-15%, and net rooms growth is expected to accelerate to 4.5-5%. The company also guided to a ~35% increase in co-branded credit card fees driven by an amended royalty rate, a structural improvement. While the U.S. & Canada RevPAR was flat in Q4 and the government shutdown was a headwind, the overall forward outlook is positive and management expressed confidence, supporting a moderately bullish score.

summary.revenue: Fourth quarter total gross fee revenues grew 7% to $1.4 billion. Full year 2025 gross fee revenues rose 5% to $5.4 billion. Total revenues for Q4 2025 were $6,690 million, up from $6,429 million in Q4 2024.
summary.eps: Fourth quarter reported diluted EPS totaled $1.65 and adjusted diluted EPS totaled $2.58. For the full year, reported diluted EPS totaled $9.51 and adjusted diluted EPS totaled $10.02.
summary.guidance: For full year 2026, the company expects worldwide RevPAR to rise 1.5% to 2.5%, net rooms growth of 4.5% to 5%, adjusted EBITDA growth of 8% to 10% (to $5.8-$5.9 billion), adjusted diluted EPS growth of 13% to 15%, and more than $4.3 billion of capital returns to shareholders. Fee revenues are expected to rise 8% to 10% to $5.9-$5.96 billion.
summary.margin: Adjusted operating income margin for Q4 2025 was 63%, compared to 62% in Q4 2024. For the full year 2025, adjusted operating income margin was 64%, compared to 63% in 2024.
key_risks: U.S. & Canada RevPAR declined 0.1% in Q4 2025, impacted by the extended government shutdown, particularly on the business transient segment.
Government RevPAR was down over 30% during the 43-day U.S. Government shutdown, moderating to down around 15%.
The operating environment in Greater China remains challenged by weak macro conditions and soft consumer sentiment.
Business transient RevPAR declined 3% in Q4 2025.
The company's guidance does not include any impact from the renegotiation of U.S. co-branded cards, as discussions are still ongoing.
Owned, leased, and other revenue net is expected to be impacted by renovations at certain large hotels, including W Barcelona and the Ritz Carlton Tokyo.
key_opportunities: International RevPAR increased 6.1% in Q4 2025 and over 5% for the full year, led by EMEA and APEC.
Luxury RevPAR increased over 6% in Q4 and for the full year, with luxury comprising 10% of both open and pipeline rooms.
The development pipeline reached a record ~610,000 rooms, up 6% year-over-year, with net rooms growth expected to accelerate to 4.5%-5% in 2026.
Co-branded credit card fees are projected to increase ~35% in 2026, driven by spending growth and an increased royalty rate.
The 2026 FIFA World Cup is expected to contribute 30-35 basis points to global RevPAR growth.
Residential branding fees are expected to increase roughly 40% in 2026.
The company is investing in AI and technology, partnering with Google and OpenAI, to enhance guest acquisition and booking.

management_tone.label: optimistic
management_tone.justification: The CEO stated, 'I am proud of the results we delivered this year and am incredibly optimistic about the future,' and the CFO described the company's 'strong financial performance' and 'strong cash-generating asset-light business model.'
